VanderGheynst, Dean, College of the Environment and Life Sciences Re: Proposal to merge Department of Landscape Architecture and Department of Geosciences Date: November 7, 2025 ————————————————————————————————————— I fully support the proposed merger of the Department of Landscape Architecture (LAR) and the Department of Geosciences (GEO).
This merger aligns with the University’s strategic goals to strengthen interdisciplinary collaboration, enhance program sustainability, and advance our land and sea grant mission.
A budget and justification summarizing how existing resources will be used is included in the submission.
The Department of Landscape Architecture offers Rhode Island’s only accredited undergraduate program of its kind and is approaching re-accreditation in 2026.
The upcoming retirement of its two tenured faculty members would leave the program without tenured or tenure-track faculty, jeopardizing accreditation.
To ensure continuity and demonstrate institutional commitment, two tenure-track faculty searches focused on Environmental Planning and Urban Design and Transportation Planning have been approved.

The merger with Geosciences, which includes several tenured and tenure-track faculty, provides the necessary structure to support new hires and ensure compliance with Article 15 of the collective bargaining agreement.
Both departments have voted in favor of the merger, recognizing the intellectual and operational benefits of joining two small, synergistic units.
Together, they will form a hub addressing climate change, resilience planning, sustainable development, and management of natural resources.
The merged department will enhance shared teaching, research, and outreach capacity while maintaining all existing academic programs without disruption or impact on other departments or colleges.
This merger represents a forward-looking investment in programs that exemplify URI’s strengths in environmental and community-based problem solving.
It supports the continued accreditation of the Bachelor of Landscape Architecture program and positions URI as a regional leader in sustainable design and Earth system science.

FACULTY SENATE OFFICE FACULTY SENATE LEGISLATION SEPTEMBER 30, 2024 Graduate Council Report 2024-2025-01A At the September 30, 2024 meeting of the Graduate Council, the following matters were considered and are now presented to the Faculty Senate for approval.
Curricular Matters Which Require Confirmation By The Faculty Senate COURSE CHANGES COLLEGE OF ARTS & SCIENCES: MUS 438 | Music, Mind and Body, Effective Spring 2025 Change in description, prerequisites, graduate credit (3 crs.) This course explores intersections of neurobiology and music, delving into the neuroscience of music stimuli and impact for health outcomes, research, and community. (Lec. 3) Pre: Music Therapy Major, Interdisciplinary Neuroscience Major Clinical Track, or by permission of instructor.
PSC 590 | Internship in Public Administration and Policy, Effective Spring 2025 Change modality, credits (1-6 crs.) Participation at a public service, non-profit, or policy organization.

Planning, policy analysis and formation, personnel management, budgeting and finance, and public service responsibilities that are the hallmark of effective governance. (Practicum/Online/Accelerated Online Course) Pre: permission of M.P.A. director.
May be taken up to 6-credits.
COLLEGE OF BUSINESS: BAI 455 | Business Analytics and Artificial Intelligence Applications, Effective Fall 2025 Change prerequisites (3 crs.) Intermediate business applications of Business Analytics and Artificial Intelligence. (Lec. 3) Pre: BAI 212, BAI356, and senior standing in a degree granting college; or by permission of instructor.
BUS 515 | Innovation and Entrepreneurship Practicum, Effective Fall 2025 Change description, modality (3 crs.) Applies business concepts in an experiential setting. (Accelerated Online Program/Practicum) Pre: open to graduate students only

MBA 526 | Product and Service Management, Effective Spring 2025 Change prerequisites (6 crs.) Project based learning to develop business ideas, market strategy, quality control, and life cycle of product and service development.
Utilizing creative design processes to deliver product innovation. (Lec. 6) MBA 529 | Career Planning, Effective Spring 2025 Change prerequisites (1 cr.) Implement career planning by researching career options, setting individual goals, preparing cover letters and resumes, and practicing for interviews. (Lec. 1) TMD 424 | Retail Product Trend Forecasting, Effective Spring 2025 Change title, description (3 crs.) Explore theory, principles, and the role of consumer trends and innovations in society from a multidisciplinary perspective and their impact on today’s global marketplace. (Lec. 3) Pre: senior or graduate standing.
COLLEGE OF THE ENVIRONMENT & LIFE SCIENCES: EEC 576 (STA576, ECN576) | Econometrics, Effective Spring 2025 Change modality, prerequisites, add cross-listings (4 crs.) Cross-listed as (EEC), ECN576, STA576.
Application of statistics and mathematics to economic analysis.

Implication of assumption required by statistical methods for testing economic hypotheses.
Current econometric methods examined and discussed. (Lec. 3, Lab. 2/Online) Pre: STA409 or equivalent, or permission of instructor.
COLLEGE OF HEALTH SCIENCE: CMD 495 (NEU495) | Snapshots of Experimental Methods in Neuroscience, Effective Spring 2025 Add cross-listing, change prerequisites (3 crs.) Crosslisted as (CMD) NEU495.
This course is designed to provide knowledge about current research methodologies within neuroscience used in research, assessment, and intervention of communication processes and disorders. (Lec. 3) Pre: NUR213, KIN122, CMD280G, CMD377, BIO220, or NEU101; junior standing, or permission of instructor.
NEU 503 (PHT503) | Introduction to the Neurosciences, Effective Spring 2025 Add cross-listing (3 crs.) Cross-listed as (NEU) PHT503.
This survey course will introduce basic neuroscience areas, including gross and microscopic anatomy, neural development, membrane physiology, sensory and motor systems, language, cognition, neuropharmacology, neuroengineering, and psychological disorders. (Lec. 3) Pre: Graduate standing or permission of the instructor.

NEW COURSES COLLEGE OF ARTS & SCIENCES: CHM 514 | Fundamentals of Mass Spectrometry, Effective Spring 2025 (3 crs.) Principles of mass spectrometry (MS).
The fundamentals of mass spectrometer will be discussed in detail as well as historic developments and MS types.
Typical analytical problems will be reviewed and examined in a laboratory setting. (Lec. 2/Lab. 1) Pre: Completion or concurrent enrollment in CHM 500, or by permission of instructor.

SCM 545 | Video Storytelling for Science and the Environment, Effective Spring 2025 (3 crs.) This course takes an interdisciplinary approach by welcoming graduate and undergraduate students from a variety of disciplines to collaborate with our project partners to create compelling science stories. (Lec. 3) COLLEGE OF BUSINESS: MBA 557 | Entrepreneurial Finance, Effective Spring 2025 (3 crs.) Introduces future entrepreneurs and managers of start-ups to the issues they will face in financial management and the valuation of a new venture through its lifecycle. (Lec. 3/Online) COLLEGE OF THE ENVIRONMENT & LIFE SCIENCES: NRS 532 (GEO 532) | Graduate Principles of Onsite Wastewater Treatment, Effective Spring 2025 (4 crs.) Cross-listed as (NRS) GEO532.
Principles of onsite wastewater treatment, including physical, chemical, biological treatment processes in soils and different system designs.

Evaluation of system performance, assessment of public and ecosystem health impacts and effects of climate change. (Lec. 3, Lab 1) COLLEGE OF PHARMACY: PHP 673 | Pharmacotherapy in Physical Therapy, Effective Summer 2025 (2 crs.) Basic principles of pharmacology, pharmacokinetics, and drug receptor function for medications that are encountered in physical therapy practice.
Students will be able to identify common classes of pharmacological agents and discuss their potential effects on a physical therapy assessment and plan of care. (Online) Pre: Doctor of Physical Therapy (DPT) student in good standing or permission from the Instructor or Department Chair COLLEGE OF EDUCATION: EDL 500 | Engaging Communities for Change, Effective Fall 2025 (3 crs.) Engage the community in school improvement, enhance communication, and transform support into advocacy.
Create a supportive school environment, promoting student success and well-being through collaborative engagement and a shared vision. (Lec. 3)

EDL 501 | Legal and Ethical Issues in Educational Leadership, Effective Fall 2025 (3 crs.) Examine the legal foundation of schools and educational policy, analyzing cases, statutes, and constitutional provisions.
Explore legal, ethical, and political issues, including due process, discipline, and rights of marginalized students. (Lec. 3) EDL 502 | Fiscal Management for Educational Leaders, Effective Fall 2025 (3 cr.) Analyze systems for financing U.S. public schools.
Examine Rhode Island’s financing, budgeting, facilities finance, purchasing, and entrepreneurship.
Prioritize legal matters, business ethics, diversity, and equity in budget allocations. (Lec. 3) EDL 503 | Operations & Management for Educational Leaders, Effective Fall 2025 (3 crs.) Integrate organizational theories and leadership models for school operations and management.
Explore resource management, school improvement planning, team engagement, and efficient school operations.
Emphasize decision-making to establish dynamic learning communities. (Lec. 3) EDL 504 | Program Evaluation for Educational Leaders, Effective Fall 2025 (3 crs.) Introduce program planning, evaluation, and data-driven decision making.

Enhance curricula and assessment programs.
Develop and assess educational programs, making informed decisions to continue, adjust, or discontinue based on evaluation evidence. (Lec. 3) EDL 505 | Supervision of Instruction, Effective Fall 2025 (3 crs.) Focus on the principal's role in enhancing classroom instruction through supervision, evaluation, and faculty development.
Explore supervisory strategies, equity, access, and engagement.
Cultivate high-performing schools with accountability, improvement, and collaboration. (Lec. 3) EDL 506 | Instructional and Curriculum Leadership, Effective Fall 2025 (3 crs.) Explore the principal's role as an instructional leader promoting collaborative culture and shared decision-making.
Align, monitor, and refine instruction and curriculum for diverse needs and standards. (Lec. 3) EDL 507 | Managing Human Capital, Effective Fall 2025 (3 crs.) Examine elements of effective human resources management for equitable teaching and learning.

Explore recruiting, hiring, development, conflict resolution, change management, and organizational climate. (Lec. 3) EDL 508 | Leading School & District Improvement, Effective Fall 2025 (3 crs.) Analyze and implement strategies for equitable educational improvements.
Emphasize data-driven decision-making, change management, culturally responsive leadership, and developing comprehensive school improvement plans. (Lec. 3) EDL 510 | Internship/Seminar I, Effective Fall 2025 (3 crs.) Engage in practical field experiences in school administration, applying RISEL standards.
Participate in seminars, reflect on experiences, and construct a leadership portfolio.
Complete 200 hours under principal and university supervision. (Internship) EDL 511 | Internship/Seminar II, Effective Fall 2025 (3 crs.) Engage in practical field experiences in school administration, applying RISEL standards.
Participate in seminars, reflect on experiences, and construct a leadership portfolio.
Complete 200 hours under principal and university supervision. (Internship)

EDL 520 | School Plant Planning, Effective Fall 2025 (3 crs.) Prepare aspiring superintendents and central office leaders in developing school building specifications. Learn planning for new and remodeled buildings, assessing facility needs, soliciting support, site selection, design, and maintenance. (Lec. 3) EDL 521 | Supervision of Special Education Programs & Services, Effective Fall 2025 (3 crs.) Examine the multifaceted responsibilities of special education leadership at the district level. Investigate budget management, staffing, instructional practices, community partnerships, assessments, legal issues, and parent involvement. (Lec. 3) GRADUATE SCHOOL OF OCEANOGRAPHY: OCG 550 | Environmental Isotope Geochemistry, Effective Fall 2025 (3 crs.) Covers fundamental isotope theory, discusses traditional and cutting-edge analytical methods, and explores isotope applications to important ecological and environmental processes across the geosphere, hydrosphere, and biosphere. (Lec. 3)

FACULTY SENATE OFFICE FACULTY SENATE LEGISLATION OCTOBER 10, 2024 Curriculum & Standards Committee Report 2024-2025-01A At the October 3, 2024 meeting of the Curriculum & Standards Committee the following matters were considered and are now presented to the Faculty Senate for approval.
Informational Matters COLLEGE OF EDUCATION: EDC 452 | Evaluation of Elementary and Middle School Students, Effective Winter 2025 Correction to typo in prerequisites (2 crs.) Purposes and means of evaluating elementary and middle school children will be critically analyzed.
Types of tests and measurement tools will be examined, such as observation checklists, sociograms, rating scales, and portfolios. (Seminar) Pre: Acceptance into the BA Elementary Education program and concurrent enrollment in EDC 423, 453 and 459.
Not for graduate credit.

Curricular Matters Which Require Confirmation By The Faculty Senate COURSE CHANGES COLLEGE OF ARTS & SCIENCES: MUS 394 | Wind Ensemble, Effective Spring 2025 Change course title (0-1 crs.) The Wind Ensemble is an auditioned ensemble that performs a diverse repertoire chosen from a variety of genres, historical eras and cultural backgrounds. (Rehearsal 3) Pre: audition and permission of instructor.
May be repeated for credit.
S/U only for 0 credit.
MTH 101 | Intermediate Algebra, Effective Spring 2025 Change method of instruction (3 crs.) Introduction to algebraic manipulation, solving equations and Inequalities in one variable.
Plotting points and graphing elementary functions.
Interpreting and expressing mathematics.
Intended for STEM majors who are not prepared to take MTH 111. (Lec. 2, Lab 2/Online) Pre: Credit for MTH099.
Not for credit for mathematics majors, not for general education credit, and not open to students with a C- or better in MTH131 or MTH141.

COLLEGE OF HEALTH SCIENCES: NUT 110 | Introduction to the Fields of Nutrition and Dietetics, Effective Fall 2025 Change course title, prerequisites (1 cr.) Description of the educational and experiential requirements of a registered dietitian and a nutritionist.
Career opportunities discussed.
Designed for students entering the nutrition and dietetics major.
Pre: Nutrition or Dietetics major or minor. (Lec. 1) NUT 336 | Scientific Principles of Food I, Effective Fall 2025 Add in-person modality (4 cr.) Chemical, physical, sensory, and nutritional properties of food related to processes used in food preparation.
Emphasis on water, carbohydrates, lipids, and the sensory evaluation of food. (Lab 2, Lec. 3/Lab 2, Online) Pre: NUT207 and NUT210 and CHM124 or CHM227.
NUT 337 | Scientific Principles of Food II, Effective Fall 2025 Add in-person modality (4 crs.) Chemical, physical, sensory, and nutritional properties of food related to processes used in food preparation.
Emphasis on proteins, scientific principles of baked goods, and research applications. (Lab 2, Lec. 3/Lab 2, Online) Pre: NUT336.

NUT 410 | Professional Issues in Nutrition and Dietetics, Effective Fall 2025 Change prerequisites (1 cr.) Professional issues in the fields of nutrition and dietetics.
Topics include career choices, graduate school, registration, licensing, and certification. (Lec. 1) Pre: Nutrition or Dietetics major or minor and senior standing or permission of instructor.
Not for graduate credit.
PSY 488 | Undergraduate Teaching Experience in Psychology, Effective Spring 2025 Change maximum credit hours, description (1-3 crs.) Students gain teaching experience assisting faculty in an on-going class, and/or preparing background materials for use in teaching. (Practicum) Pre: permission of instructor.
May be repeated for 6 credits total.
Not for graduate credit.
COLLEGE OF PHARMACY: BPS 426 | cGMP Environmental Risks, Control and Monitoring, Effective Spring 2025 Change method of instruction, prerequisites (3 crs.) Principles of clean room design and operations for the pharmaceutical and biotechnology industry.
Reviews clean room operations and monitoring fundamentals.

Monitoring and sampling will be performed in a cGMP environment. (Lec. 2, Lab 1) Pre: Students enrolled in Pharmaceutical Sciences BS, Pharmacy PMD, Pharmaceutical Manufacturing & Formulation Minor, or Biomedical and Pharmaceutical Sciences Minor, or by permission of instructor.
Not for graduate credit.
